interventions.action: Rendered the docs pages (/install, /build-a-screen, /support, /cli and the card, select, field, input, badge, empty and dialog component pages) with a local headless Chromium through Playwright, with TMPDIR=/tmp, to read their text and the source in their Code tabs. interventions.reason: Those pages are a client-rendered SPA, so curl returned only an empty HTML shell. Chromium aborted under the default TMPDIR because its socket path was too long. /llms.txt was readable as plain text, but it links to these pages for the lint fragment, the theme steps and the example source.

interventions.action: Moved @stylexjs/stylex, @stylexjs/babel-plugin and @stylexjs/postcss-plugin from 0.19.0, as init pinned them, to 0.19.1 to match @stylexjs/eslint-plugin 0.19.1: npm install --save-exact @stylexjs/stylex@0.19.1, then npm install -D --save-exact @stylexjs/babel-plugin@0.19.1 @stylexjs/postcss-plugin@0.19.1 @stylexjs/eslint-plugin@0.19.1.
interventions.reason: The install page says to install eslint-plugin 0.19.1. With that version, doctor reported ULT-LINT-003 and printed a repair that downgrades the plugin to 0.19.0. I applied that repair, and ESLint then failed with two valid-styles errors on the installed components/ui/select.tsx (gridColumn: 2). No printed guidance covered upgrading the compiler packages. The Support page lists 0.19.1 as the tested version for both Next.js layouts.

interventions.action: Removed the scaffold's next/font/google Geist and Geist_Mono loading, its className and the create-next-app metadata from app/layout.tsx, and added the import of ../ultima-theme.css after ./ultima.css.
interventions.reason: The theme import is documented. Removing Geist is not: the scaffold loaded those fonts from Google, and no Ultima token reads them.

interventions.action: Downloaded the theme registry item JSON from the public host into scratch/theme-dl and compared its DESIGN.md content byte for byte with the installed file. Also tried hashing several candidate regions against the recorded content digest.
interventions.reason: npx ultima-design doctor --theme exits 1 with 'mismatch DESIGN.md: generated region digest: expected intact, actual edited', even though DESIGN.md was never edited. The installed file is identical to what the registry serves, so the export's recorded digest disagrees with the CLI's digest. I did not hand-patch the digest. DESIGN.md is left exactly as installed.

decisions.choice: Aligned every StyleX package on 0.19.1: stylex, babel-plugin, postcss-plugin and eslint-plugin.
options: Keep stylex 0.19.0 with eslint-plugin 0.19.1, as the install page tested it: lint passes, but doctor reports advisory ULT-LINT-003 (the versions differ)
Downgrade eslint-plugin to 0.19.0, doctor's printed repair: the versions match, but ESLint errors on the installed select.tsx

Upgrade the compiler packages to 0.19.1, the Support page's tested Next.js versions: lint passes, and doctor reports advisory ULT-SETUP-017 ('above the CLI's tested 0.19.0; nothing to do if it works')
decisions.why: Every option leaves a non-blocking advisory. Only the third gives a clean lint run and matches the versions in the Support page's tested matrix, and the production build and the browser checks pass on it.

decisions.choice: Accepted the theme's documented font fallback (the system-ui stack after 'Figtree') and loaded no font files.
options: Load Figtree and IBM Plex Mono with next/font/google
Self-host the font files
Accept the stack's fallback and remove the scaffold's unused Geist loading
decisions.why: The export loads no faces, and the guidance allows accepting the fallback. The brief limits this run to the public host, so fetching Google Fonts was out. The Geist faces the scaffold loaded were never read by any token.

decisions.choice: Put the screen's breakpoint in its own token module as stylex.defineConsts (media.wide = '@media (min-width: 52rem)'), next to the app's size variables (content max width, page minimum height) in components/pantry/pantry.stylex.ts.
options: A named module constant inside pantry.tsx, as the llms.txt principle and the Projects example do
defineConsts in the application's token module
decisions.why: The brief allows no lengths outside the theme and token modules. defineConsts can be used as a media-query key, and doing it this way passes both StyleX lint and ultima-design check.

decisions.choice: Built stock-list rows on the Card 'Item' recipe (a text stack, the quantity, and a trailing Button). The Button switches from outline to solid and sets aria-pressed for the selected item, and the app paints no selected-row surface of its own.
options: Item recipe rows with a trailing Button that carries the selection state
The whole row as a ghost Button with its height and layout overridden
A Table with a View action column
decisions.why: The recipe treats rows as static and makes a control the thing that acts. Changing the Button variant shows the selection in the brand accent without overriding any component style.

decisions.choice: Accent Badge for the category, warning Badge for low stock (under 5), and the accent tone on the selected item's button and the submit button.
options: Neutral badges everywhere
Accent for brand emphasis and warning for low stock
Accent for low stock
decisions.why: The brief wants the berry as the product's accent but out of status meaning. Low stock is a status, so it keeps the warning role.

decisions.choice: Left the theme in system mode: no data-theme attribute and no mode toggle.
options: System mode
Pin data-theme to dark or light
Add the Theme Mode item with a user toggle
decisions.why: The generated CSS supplies full dark and light values and follows the system preference, and the guidance says not to add a separate mode switch for the artifact. Both explicit modes were also verified by setting data-theme in the production build.

review.rule: An intervention is an action on the project or its tooling that the guidance or CLI output did not print or link. A decision is a choice about setting up, theming or styling with Ultima that the guidance did not settle and that changed the output; product choices the brief leaves open (data, copy, arrangement, Select or Dialog) and choices between documented options are not counted. Running git init and ultima install, which init's report prints, follows the guidance.
